supports: nameLen and bufSize are int; nameLen is sizeof(XML_Char) * (strLen + 1) and bufSize adds ROUND_UP(rawNameLength, sizeof(XML_Char))
no overflow check exists before the comparison bufSize > tag->bufEnd - tag->buf
when the sum wraps, the comparison can be false, the REALLOC is skipped, and memcpy(rawNameBuf, tag->rawName, tag->rawNameLength) writes out of bounds
rawNameBuf is tag->buf + nameLen, i.e. past the allocation when the buffer was sized for the wrapped value
the fixed code computes rawNameLen as size_t and checks rawNameLen > (size_t)INT_MAX - nameLen before computing bufSize
on overflow it returns XML_FALSE, which the callers turn into XML_ERROR_NO_MEMORY
the memcpy is only reached when bufSize is a correct int and the buffer has been enlarged if needed
the commit message states the overflow permits out-of-bounds heap writes and that the default configuration is affected
it notes XML_UNICODE builds are not exploitable because XML_Char is wider

it explains the three-part PoC: a short root node to move m_buffer just below a power of two, a tag name below the INT_MAX/2 string-pool limit, and UTF-16 encoding of ASCII to double the raw byte count
the diff adds the size_t check and the INT_MAX subtraction guard

critical_operation.description: storeRawNames sizes the tag buffer as int nameLen + ROUND_UP(rawNameLength, sizeof(XML_Char)). Both terms are derived from attacker-controlled tag-name lengths; their sum can wrap past INT_MAX. When it does, bufSize compares as small enough for the existing allocation, so REALLOC is skipped, but the following memcpy still copies rawNameLength bytes to tag->buf + nameLen, writing past the heap allocation. The 2.4.5 fix detects rawNameLen > (size_t)INT_MAX - nameLen and returns XML_FALSE.

entry_point.description: contentProcessor runs doContent and then calls storeRawNames to move each open tag raw name out of the about-to-be-discarded parse buffer. The raw name and the pool-allocated name come from the XML document; the fix commit explains that a UTF-16 document of roughly 2/3 INT_MAX bytes with a short root node reaches the overflow.
